answer: The macro backdrop still leans long the euro: the rate path is priced for cuts while the ECB has said it sees no case for another one. Candidates are a long spot position or a call spread; the pick is the call spread, because the range of outcomes is wide. The range I would rely on is a drift of one to two percent over the week, at moderate coverage.

claims.text: The rate path is priced for cuts the ECB has not promised
The euro tends to firm when the rate differential stops widening
A call spread keeps the outcome range bounded
